cells.tense: You're here, in the hundredth repetition, and you're actually looking at it.
cells.verb: seeing freshly, before you've decided what you're looking at
cells.place: in the practice you keep alone, by repetition
cells.ask: take one clear look at the work this week and let it stay a look — no correction, no note, just the seeing; the practice already shines because it's yours, not because anyone's watching
cells.core:
You're here, in the hundredth repetition, and you're actually looking at it. Most people stop seeing the thing they practice — the hands go on, the eyes go elsewhere. Yours haven't. Each pass arrives a little new, and the small steady light you keep lit is lit by that noticing, not by effort. That's why the work keeps refining instead of just repeating.

If you want somewhere for this to go: take one clear look at the work this week and let it stay a look — no correction, no note, just the seeing. You don't have to make use of everything you see. The practice already shines because it's yours, not because anyone's watching.
cells.sheetLine: You still see what you practice, and that's what keeps it alive.

cells.tense: You're already seeing the flaw in a repetition you haven't finished.
cells.verb: seeing freshly, before you've decided what you're looking at
cells.place: in the practice you keep alone, by repetition
cells.ask: do the next pass as if it were the first — carry only what your hands already know, nothing you've pre-decided about how it will go wrong; the work lights up when you're in it, not when you've proven you can see it
cells.core:
You're already seeing the flaw in a repetition you haven't finished. The clarity is real — it's just arriving ahead of the work, so every pass gets inspected before it's done and nothing gets to simply be practiced. You're living in the version where you've finally caught every error, and the catching has become the practice. Seeing that sharp, that early, leaves no room for the hands to find anything on their own.

The way back isn't to see less. It's to do the next pass as if it were the first — carry only what your hands already know, nothing you've pre-decided about how it will go wrong. Let one repetition be fresh before it's judged. The work lights up when you're in it, not when you've proven you can see it.
cells.sheetLine: You're catching the mistake before you've made it, and it's costing you the practice.

cells.tense: You stopped looking at this a while back, and the hands kept going without you.
cells.verb: seeing freshly, before you've decided what you're looking at
cells.place: in the practice you keep alone, by repetition
cells.ask: pick one thing you've been drilling and carry it all the way to finished — on purpose, by your own choice, this week; finishing it will show you where you actually stand, and the seeing comes back on its own once you're standing in the work
cells.core:
You stopped looking at this a while back, and the hands kept going without you. The repetitions still happen — you're not lazy, you're showing up — but you're running them on an old picture of where you were, and nothing new is getting in. The small light is still lit. It's just not being looked at, so it isn't showing you anything.

Don't try to force fresh eyes onto the drill; staring harder at an empty seat doesn't fill it. Instead, pick one thing you've been drilling and carry it all the way to finished — on purpose, by your own choice, this week. Getting it done will show you where you actually stand. Once you're standing in the work rather than behind it, the seeing comes back on its own, and the practice shines because it's yours again.
cells.sheetLine: You're still practicing. You just stopped watching.

cells.tense: You already see exactly where it's off, and you're calling that muscle memory.
cells.verb: seeing freshly, before you've decided what you're looking at
cells.place: in the practice you keep alone, by repetition
cells.ask: say "I saw that" about one adjustment you've been calling automatic — just the noticing, before the fixing; you shine because you see, not because you can prove it
cells.core:
You already see exactly where it's off, and you're calling that muscle memory. Every adjustment you make mid-repetition — the small catch, the course correction nobody taught you — comes from a clear look you took and then handed the credit to the drill. The seeing is yours. It's running every time you practice, and you talk about it as if the work corrects itself.

The move is smaller than it sounds: say "I saw that" about one adjustment you've been calling automatic. Just the noticing, before the fixing. You don't have to make anything of it. You shine because you see, not because you can prove it.
cells.sheetLine: You're already seeing it. You've been calling it the drill.
